en/blog/1930s-fashion-silhouette-guide.h.old: The decade extends beyond Hollywood gowns. Daytime clothing included natural-waisted dresses, shoulder-defined suits, below-knee skirts, knits and practical separates. At night, low-backed satin bias-cut gowns created body-skimming lines without relying on heavily rigid shaping.

Madeleine Vionnet experimented with it in the 1920s; the V&A describes her role in championing free-flowing garments shaped around the body.

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: Retrofuturism can be understood as revisiting past visions of the future. Atompunk focuses on the atomic age and space exploration. Material introduced by Bruce Sterling in WIRED centers on the pre-digital period of 1945–1965, with connections to mid-century design, Googie architecture and Space Age references.

en/blog/atompunk.html.heading: How does Atompunk look at the future through the past?

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: That timeframe provides a useful reference area, not an absolute boundary for every work. More important is how you read the imagery: smooth curves, orbital shapes, starbursts or surfaces recalling old equipment can communicate a future once imagined.

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: Atompunk-inspired clothing today therefore does not mean what everyone actually wore in the 1950s. One is an aesthetic interpretation; the other is dress history. The guide to 1950s women's fashion helps when you want to understand that period's silhouettes separately.

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: Nor should one game or film become the sole definition. A work may blend several influences to build its world. For an outfit, choose one clear visual idea, such as circles and silver, then develop around it.

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: Atompunk and Dieselpunk can both occupy the intersection of nostalgia and science fiction. In common usage, Dieselpunk tends toward industrial machinery, engines and an early-twentieth-century atmosphere; Atompunk leans toward atomic-age visions of the future. Boundaries can vary between writers.

en/blog/atompunk.html.old: For styling, compare the emphasis instead of classifying through one color. Straps, worn leather, goggles and mechanical details tend to suggest a machine-centered world. Streamlined shapes, bright surfaces and orbital forms make atomic or space references easier to read.

You can borrow these elements for Atompunk without treating the two concepts as identical.

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Simple for everyday wear: Try a black tiered skirt, white tee, sneakers, and a plain bag. Keep the sleeves fairly slim and adjust the hem so the first tier shows clearly. This makes it easier to see how the skirt fits.

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Soft with closely related colors: Try a cream skirt, a simple cream or pale pink top, and a short cardigan if needed. Add a different finish in the buttons or shoes to distinguish the pieces. If every piece has ruffles, try removing one before changing the palette.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: Soft with closely related colors: Try a cream skirt, a simple cream or pale pink top, and a short cardigan if needed. en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Dark with texture: Try a black tiered skirt, slim black top, and boots you can move in. The shape of the tiers becomes the main detail. A small metal accent can add a spot of brightness if you want one.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: Dark with texture: Try a black tiered skirt, slim black top, and boots you can move in. The shape of the tiers becomes the main detail. A small metal accent can add a spot of brightness if you want one.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Three ways to style the same skirt

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Use these combinations as starting points. Substitute clothes you own with a similar shape. Try them first to see whether you actually need another color or a different cut.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: Use these combinations as starting points. Substitute clothes you own with a similar shape. Try them first to see whether you actually need another color or a different cut.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Three ways to style the same skirt

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Try a short skirt in the positions you’ll use during the day. Sit down, step onto a low stair, and bend as you normally would to check coverage. Check the lining or built-in shorts if the skirt has them.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: Try a short skirt in the positions you’ll use during the day. Sit down, step onto a low stair, and bend as you normally would to check coverage. Check the lining or built-in shorts if the skirt has them.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Check the outfit as you sit, walk, and carry things

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: If a tier rolls or catches, see whether it’s touching the bag, a jacket zipper, or fabric tucked into the waistband. If the waistband twists, check the fit before adding a pin or belt. Choose a fit that stays put without constant adjustment.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: If a tier rolls or catches, see whether it’s touching the bag, a jacket zipper, or fabric tucked into the waistband. If the waistband twists, check the fit before adding a pin or belt. Choose a fit that stays put without constant adjustment.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Check the outfit as you sit, walk, and carry things

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: If the outfit feels busy, change one thing at a time. Try a plain top, a slimmer sleeve, or a different bag. Keep the combinations that let the tiers show clearly while you move comfortably.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: If the outfit feels busy, change one thing at a time. Try a plain top, a slimmer sleeve, or a different bag. Keep the combinations that let the tiers show clearly while you move comfortably.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Check the outfit as you sit, walk, and carry things

en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.old: Before buying another top, record the hem length and width you like in the outfit you’ve tried. Compare measurements with a top that fits you. Try the new piece on if you can, since drape and sleeves can change how two tops of the same length look.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.text: Before buying another top, record the hem length and width you like in the outfit you’ve tried. Compare measurements with a top that fits you. Try the new piece on if you can, since drape and sleeves can change how two tops of the same length look.
en/blog/cach-phoi-do-voi-chan-vay-tang-n.heading: Check the outfit as you sit, walk, and carry things

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: The shirt should be long enough to stay inside the waistband when you sit and reach overhead. A very short shirt may work better untucked. A long, thick shirt can create bulk. The right technique depends on how the shirt is made.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: The shirt should be long enough to stay inside the waistband when you sit and reach overhead. A very short shirt may work better untucked. A long, thick shirt can create bulk. The right technique depends on how the shirt is made.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Check the shirt and waistband first

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Look at whether the hem is straight or curved, whether there are side vents, and how the front and back lengths compare. A long curved hem usually gives you plenty of fabric to tuck, but you’ll need to distribute it evenly. A short straight hem may work with a small front tuck if there’s enough length.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Look at whether the hem is straight or curved, whether there are side vents, and how the front and back lengths compare. A long curved hem usually gives you plenty of fabric to tuck, but you’ll need to distribute it evenly. A short straight hem may work with a small front tuck if there’s enough length.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Check the shirt and waistband first

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: The waistband of your trousers or skirt needs room for the tucked layer as well as your waist. If it feels tight once fastened, another tuck may do little to fix the fit. Choose a combination that still lets you move comfortably.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: The waistband of your trousers or skirt needs room for the tucked layer as well as your waist. If it feels tight once fastened, another tuck may do little to fix the fit. Choose a combination that still lets you move comfortably.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Check the shirt and waistband first

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: In the mirror, let the button placket sit in its natural position. Pulling it to one side can distort the shirt. If the shirt already strains across the bust or shoulders, address the fit first. Our women’s tops guide explains how to read the cut before choosing how to wear it.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: In the mirror, let the button placket sit in its natural position. Pulling it to one side can distort the shirt. If the shirt already strains across the bust or shoulders, address the fit first. Our women’s tops guide explains how to read the cut before choosing how to wear it.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Check the shirt and waistband first

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: How much fabric to pull out depends on the shirt. Soft fabric may fall gently over the waistband, while crisp fabric forms a more defined fold. You should be able to reach forward without pulling the neckline down and sit without feeling the shirt stretch from shoulder to waist.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: How much fabric to pull out depends on the shirt. Soft fabric may fall gently over the waistband, while crisp fabric forms a more defined fold. You should be able to reach forward without pulling the neckline down and sit without feeling the shirt stretch from shoulder to waist.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Full tuck: Work in sections to avoid bulk

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: If the back balloons, open the waistband and smooth it out again. Pulling hard from the front may shift the shoulders or placket. Check both hips while adjusting so you don’t move all the excess from one place to another.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: If the back balloons, open the waistband and smooth it out again. Pulling hard from the front may shift the shoulders or placket. Check both hips while adjusting so you don’t move all the excess from one place to another.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Full tuck: Work in sections to avoid bulk

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: A full tuck works when you want the waistline visible or a tidy finish. For work, choose according to the shirt and the dress code. A thick shirt left untucked at the right length can look more polished than fabric crammed around the waist.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: A full tuck works when you want the waistline visible or a tidy finish. For work, choose according to the shirt and the dress code. A thick shirt left untucked at the right length can look more polished than fabric crammed around the waist.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Full tuck: Work in sections to avoid bulk

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Start at the center front. Tuck in part of the hem and smooth it gently toward either side. Let the back hang naturally and adjust the transition at the hips to avoid bunching. Fasten the waistband and ease out enough fabric to keep the shirt from pulling diagonally.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Start at the center front. Tuck in part of the hem and smooth it gently toward either side. Let the back hang naturally and adjust the transition at the hips to avoid bunching. Fasten the waistband and ease out enough fabric to keep the shirt from pulling diagonally.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Front tuck: Show the waistband and leave the back loose

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: If the shirt is very loose, start with a small section at the front and tuck in more if you prefer the look. If the sides keep sticking up, check the hem shape and fabric thickness. The shirt may work better fully tucked or left loose.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: If the shirt is very loose, start with a small section at the front and tuck in more if you prefer the look. If the sides keep sticking up, check the hem shape and fabric thickness. The shirt may work better fully tucked or left loose.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Front tuck: Show the waistband and leave the back loose

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Look from the side to see whether the back hangs lower than you want. A front tuck leaves the original volume in the shoulders, sleeves, and back. If the outfit still has too much fabric for your taste, check the pants shape or shirt length as well.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Look from the side to see whether the back hangs lower than you want. A front tuck leaves the original volume in the shoulders, sleeves, and back. If the outfit still has too much fabric for your taste, check the pants shape or shirt length as well.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Front tuck: Show the waistband and leave the back loose

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: If your trousers have a prominent zipper, button, or belt, see whether the tuck covers or pushes it out of place. The waistband is a focal point here, so how the fabric sits there matters more than making the two sides identical.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: If your trousers have a prominent zipper, button, or belt, see whether the tuck covers or pushes it out of place. The waistband is a focal point here, so how the fabric sits there matters more than making the two sides identical.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Front tuck: Show the waistband and leave the back loose

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: A one-sided tuck needs two front panels that can separate easily at the hem. If you need to undo the bottom buttons, open only as many as the design and your preferred coverage allow. Sit down to check for gaps and watch for strain on the placket.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: A one-sided tuck needs two front panels that can separate easily at the hem. If you need to undo the bottom buttons, open only as many as the design and your preferred coverage allow. Sit down to check for gaps and watch for strain on the placket.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: One-sided tuck: Choose a shirt that opens at the hem

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Tuck one front panel into the waistband and leave the other out. Adjust the placket and the point where the two sides meet so the shirt doesn’t twist. Try each side if you carry a bag or have a detail on the trousers you want to show.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Tuck one front panel into the waistband and leave the other out. Adjust the placket and the point where the two sides meet so the shirt doesn’t twist. Try each side if you carry a bag or have a detail on the trousers you want to show.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: One-sided tuck: Choose a shirt that opens at the hem

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Use this tuck when you want an asymmetrical shape. If the untucked panel covers most of the trousers or keeps catching on a pocket, try another approach. The outfit still needs to work while you walk, sit, or carry a bag.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Use this tuck when you want an asymmetrical shape. If the untucked panel covers most of the trousers or keeps catching on a pocket, try another approach. The outfit still needs to work while you walk, sit, or carry a bag.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: One-sided tuck: Choose a shirt that opens at the hem

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: After tucking in, find the extra fabric on each side. Open the waistband if needed, smooth each side, and make a small fold toward the back. Hold the folds while fastening the waist, then ease a little fabric back out so the shirt can move with you.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: After tucking in, find the extra fabric on each side. Open the waistband if needed, smooth each side, and make a small fold toward the back. Hold the folds while fastening the waist, then ease a little fabric back out so the shirt can move with you.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Fold excess fabric at the sides of a loose shirt

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Keep the folds small enough that the side seams stay in place and the front placket doesn’t pull open. This method works with a moderate amount of extra fabric. If you’re folding several thick layers, the shirt may be too wide or the fabric too bulky for this tuck.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Keep the folds small enough that the side seams stay in place and the front placket doesn’t pull open. This method works with a moderate amount of extra fabric. If you’re folding several thick layers, the shirt may be too wide or the fabric too bulky for this tuck.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Fold excess fabric at the sides of a loose shirt

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Check how the folds look through thinner trousers or skirts. A fold may show as a ridge at the hip. If so, tuck in less, try a front tuck, or choose bottoms with different construction. Tightening the waistband can make the ridge more visible.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Check how the folds look through thinner trousers or skirts. A fold may show as a ridge at the hip. If so, tuck in less, try a front tuck, or choose bottoms with different construction. Tightening the waistband can make the ridge more visible.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Fold excess fabric at the sides of a loose shirt

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: With a thick shirt, skip the side folds and try it untucked before buying roomier trousers. See how the pieces you already own work together before adding new ones just to manage extra fabric.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: With a thick shirt, skip the side folds and try it untucked before buying roomier trousers. See how the pieces you already own work together before adding new ones just to manage extra fabric.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Fold excess fabric at the sides of a loose shirt

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Soft, drapey fabric: Smooth each tail to avoid a bulky spot. After tucking, look from the side to see whether the shirt drapes the way you want. Leave the natural folds if you like them and fix areas that are rolled or twisted.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Soft, drapey fabric: Smooth each tail to avoid a bulky spot. After tucking, look from the side to see whether the shirt drapes the way you want. Leave the natural folds if you like them and fix areas that are rolled or twisted.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Adjust for drape, thickness, and length

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Crisp fabric: Use fewer folds and place them deliberately. A wide, crisp shirt can create volume around the waist even when smoothed flat. Try a front tuck or a small side fold, then judge it with the trousers on.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Crisp fabric: Use fewer folds and place them deliberately. A wide, crisp shirt can create volume around the waist even when smoothed flat. Try a front tuck or a small side fold, then judge it with the trousers on.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Adjust for drape, thickness, and length

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Thick fabric: Limit how much you put into the waistband. If you struggle to fasten it or sit comfortably, wear the shirt another way. A tuck should stay comfortable once you start moving.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Thick fabric: Limit how much you put into the waistband. If you struggle to fasten it or sit comfortably, wear the shirt another way. A tuck should stay comfortable once you start moving.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Adjust for drape, thickness, and length

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Long shirt: Distribute the fabric around your waist so the tails don’t all sit at the front. If the shirt is longer than you need, try wearing it loose, using it as an outer layer, or having it shortened if appropriate. Try a different tuck before cutting it.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Long shirt: Distribute the fabric around your waist so the tails don’t all sit at the front. If the shirt is longer than you need, try wearing it loose, using it as an outer layer, or having it shortened if appropriate. Try a different tuck before cutting it.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Adjust for drape, thickness, and length

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Check whether the shirt is long enough and whether the shoulders and armholes allow you to reach. A deeper tuck won’t add length or room at the shoulders. Ease out a little more fabric, change the tuck, or choose another shirt if you’ll be reaching a lot that day.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Check whether the shirt is long enough and whether the shoulders and armholes allow you to reach. A deeper tuck won’t add length or room at the shoulders. Ease out a little more fabric, change the tuck, or choose another shirt if you’ll be reaching a lot that day.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: The shirt comes untucked when you lift your arms

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Open the waistband and smooth the tails again. Look for rolled fabric or overlapping layers at the center. Spread some excess toward the sides, then check for bulk at the hips. If the waistband is already tight, try a different size or wear the shirt another way.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Open the waistband and smooth the tails again. Look for rolled fabric or overlapping layers at the center. Spread some excess toward the sides, then check for bulk at the hips. If the waistband is already tight, try a different size or wear the shirt another way.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: The front feels bulky

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Adjust the shirt from the shoulders down before changing the tuck. One tail pushed in too far can twist the body. A tight fit can also strain the buttons. Fix the source of the pull before adding a belt.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Adjust the shirt from the shoulders down before changing the tuck. One tail pushed in too far can twist the body. A tight fit can also strain the buttons. Fix the source of the pull before adding a belt.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: The placket twists and the buttons pull

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Check a side and back photo to see where the fabric sits. Smooth the back toward the sides before making any folds. A little fullness can be intentional. Adjust the parts that differ from the look you want.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Check a side and back photo to see where the fabric sits. Smooth the back toward the sides before making any folds. A little fullness can be intentional. Adjust the parts that differ from the look you want.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: The back balloons while the front looks neat

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Sit in a chair, get up, walk a few steps, and reach for something on a table. Check the waistband, placket, and back afterward. If every movement calls for a full adjustment, try a different tuck before going out.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Sit in a chair, get up, walk a few steps, and reach for something on a table. Check the waistband, placket, and back afterward. If every movement calls for a full adjustment, try a different tuck before going out.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Test the tuck against your plans for the day

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: If you’ll wear a jacket, check whether the shirt pulls loose as you slide your arms into the sleeves. Our guide to layering women’s outfits explains how the inner and outer layers work together. Check the tuck on its own first so the outfit works when the jacket comes off.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: If you’ll wear a jacket, check whether the shirt pulls loose as you slide your arms into the sleeves. Our guide to layering women’s outfits explains how the inner and outer layers work together. Check the tuck on its own first so the outfit works when the jacket comes off.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Test the tuck against your plans for the day

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: For a day sitting at school or work, try a full tuck with a shirt long enough to stay in place and enough ease to move. For a relaxed outing, a front tuck can work with a moderately loose shirt. Try a one-sided tuck if you want asymmetry and have checked your coverage while seated.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: For a day sitting at school or work, try a full tuck with a shirt long enough to stay in place and enough ease to move. For a relaxed outing, a front tuck can work with a moderately loose shirt. Try a one-sided tuck if you want asymmetry and have checked your coverage while seated.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Choose a tuck you can maintain

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: To choose the trousers by silhouette first, see our women’s pants guide. Once you have a tuck that works, our guide to what pants to wear with a women’s shirt can help you choose the cut, color, and shoes.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: To choose the trousers by silhouette first, see our women’s pants guide . Once you have a tuck that works, our guide to what pants to wear with a women’s shirt can help you choose the cut, color, and shoes.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Choose a tuck you can maintain

en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.old: Remember the method that feels comfortable and needs the fewest adjustments with your shirt. You can tuck one shirt several ways, and some methods will work better than others. Testing the tuck in motion makes it easier to choose next time.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.text: Remember the method that feels comfortable and needs the fewest adjustments with your shirt. You can tuck one shirt several ways, and some methods will work better than others. Testing the tuck in motion makes it easier to choose next time.
en/blog/cach-so-vin-ao-so-mi.html.heading: Choose a tuck you can maintain

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: Lay the scarf out and look at its shape and edges. A long, narrow scarf may be ready to wear. Fold a wide rectangular scarf lengthwise into a band. Keep the folds loose and even so it’s easy to adjust later.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: Lay the scarf out and look at its shape and edges. A long, narrow scarf may be ready to wear. Fold a wide rectangular scarf lengthwise into a band. Keep the folds loose and even so it’s easy to adjust later.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Choose the width of the scarf before tying it

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: If it has fringe, check for tangles and see whether it catches on jewelry. If it has a colored border, fold it so the border shows along the edge. Turning the scarf over or changing the fold width can change the look with the same knot.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: If it has fringe, check for tangles and see whether it catches on jewelry. If it has a colored border, fold it so the border shows along the edge. Turning the scarf over or changing the fold width can change the look with the same knot.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Choose the width of the scarf before tying it

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: Thickness determines the size of the knot. A chunky knit usually works better with fewer wraps than a knot with several layers. A thin scarf can make a compact knot, but a smooth finish can slip. Check it against the garment you plan to wear.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: Thickness determines the size of the knot. A chunky knit usually works better with fewer wraps than a knot with several layers. A thin scarf can make a compact knot, but a smooth finish can slip. Check it against the garment you plan to wear.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Choose the width of the scarf before tying it

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: Our guide to choosing a women’s scarf covers fabric, dimensions, and intended use. With the scarf in hand, decide whether you want warmth, a vertical line, or a touch of color around the neck.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: Our guide to choosing a women’s scarf covers fabric, dimensions, and intended use. With the scarf in hand, decide whether you want warmth, a vertical line, or a touch of color around the neck.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Choose the width of the scarf before tying it

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: The open drape leaves the print and length visible. Two hanging ends create vertical lines over a plain top. If it keeps slipping off as you walk, try a wrap or loop to hold it in place.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: The open drape leaves the print and length visible. Two hanging ends create vertical lines over a plain top. If it keeps slipping off as you walk, try a wrap or loop to hold it in place.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Open drape: let both ends show their length

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: With a V-neck, the ends can follow the opening. A scarf adds bulk to an already covered area on a high neck, so try a lighter one if it bunches. Leave the ends uneven if you like the effect.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: With a V-neck, the ends can follow the opening. A scarf adds bulk to an already covered area on a high neck, so try a lighter one if it bunches. Leave the ends uneven if you like the effect.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Open drape: let both ends show their length

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: The longer end needs enough length to go all the way around and still hang where you want. If it comes up short, start with a bigger difference between the ends or use the open drape. Leave the wrap loose even if tightening it would gain a few centimeters at the ends.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: The longer end needs enough length to go all the way around and still hang where you want. If it comes up short, start with a bigger difference between the ends or use the open drape. Leave the wrap loose even if tightening it would gain a few centimeters at the ends.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Single wrap: start with one end longer

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A thick scarf gives the wrap a fuller shape that can work over a simple top. A thin scarf drapes more softly and leaves more of the neckline visible. Move the crossover slightly off-center if you’d like the focus to one side.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A thick scarf gives the wrap a fuller shape that can work over a simple top. A thin scarf drapes more softly and leaves more of the neckline visible. Move the crossover slightly off-center if you’d like the focus to one side.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Single wrap: start with one end longer

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: To take it off, loosen the wrap and unwind the end in the reverse direction. Pulling sharply on one end can tighten the scarf before it comes free. Practice removing it gently, especially if it has fringe or a surface that catches easily.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: To take it off, loosen the wrap and unwind the end in the reverse direction. Pulling sharply on one end can tighten the scarf before it comes free. Practice removing it gently, especially if it has fringe or a surface that catches easily.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Single wrap: start with one end longer

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: This style is easy to make and uses some of the scarf’s length at the loop. On a short scarf, the ends may hang only a little. A very thick scarf will make a bulky knot. Try a single wrap or an open drape if either is easier to wear.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: This style is easy to make and uses some of the scarf’s length at the loop. On a short scarf, the ends may hang only a little. A very thick scarf will make a bulky knot. Try a single wrap or an open drape if either is easier to wear.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Folded loop: pull both ends through together

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: With a reversible scarf, set the colors you want to show on the loop and the tails before pulling them through. Adjusting after tightening can twist the layers. Keep the loop loose enough to show its shape and remove it easily.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: With a reversible scarf, set the colors you want to show on the loop and the tails before pulling them through. Adjusting after tightening can twist the layers. Keep the loop loose enough to show its shape and remove it easily.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Folded loop: pull both ends through together

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: The folded loop creates a cluster at the front of the neck. Try it with a simple neckline. If the top already has a large bow or ruffle, the open drape gives each detail more space.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: The folded loop creates a cluster at the front of the neck. Try it with a simple neckline. If the top already has a large bow or ruffle, the open drape gives each detail more space.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Folded loop: pull both ends through together

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A low knot leaves more space between the neck and the tie. A high knot draws attention toward the face, so check for bulk. If a slippery scarf keeps coming undone when you move, try a different style and keep the knot loose.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A low knot leaves more space between the neck and the tie. A high knot draws attention toward the face, so check for bulk. If a slippery scarf keeps coming undone when you move, try a different style and keep the knot loose.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Off-center single knot for a thin or narrow scarf

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A small print makes the knot easy to see against a plain top. If the top has a print too, use a shared color or lower the contrast in one pattern. Step back to see how the patterns work across the whole outfit.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A small print makes the knot easy to see against a plain top. If the top has a print too, use a shared color or lower the contrast in one pattern. Step back to see how the patterns work across the whole outfit.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Off-center single knot for a thin or narrow scarf

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A soft, light scarf works best for a bow. Practice on a flat surface to see whether you have enough length and whether the knot feels too bulky. If the band is wide, fold it narrower without twisting it into a cord.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A soft, light scarf works best for a bow. Practice on a flat surface to see whether you have enough length and whether the knot feels too bulky. If the band is wide, fold it narrower without twisting it into a cord.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Small bow for a long, lightweight scarf

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A slightly uneven bow can look intentional. Check whether the knot stays in place. If it needs constant adjustment, a single knot or folded loop may be easier to wear to class or work.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A slightly uneven bow can look intentional. Check whether the knot stays in place. If it needs constant adjustment, a single knot or folded loop may be easier to wear to class or work.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Small bow for a long, lightweight scarf

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: A bow adds volume at the neckline. Try wearing fewer necklaces or skip long earrings that touch the scarf. Our guide to statement accessories for women helps you pick a focal point when hair, glasses, and a scarf are all near your face.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: A bow adds volume at the neckline. Try wearing fewer necklaces or skip long earrings that touch the scarf. Our guide to statement accessories for women helps you pick a focal point when hair, glasses, and a scarf are all near your face.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Small bow for a long, lightweight scarf

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: With a button-up, decide how much of the collar to show. A low knot and narrow band usually keep the collar clearer than a thick wrap. Turn your head and check whether the scarf pushes up the top button area or collar points.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: With a button-up, decide how much of the collar to show. A low knot and narrow band usually keep the collar clearer than a thick wrap. Turn your head and check whether the scarf pushes up the top button area or collar points.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Work with the neckline you’re wearing

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: With a V-neck cardigan, the ends can follow the opening. If the cardigan is buttoned up, a large knot may sit directly over the buttons. Move it off-center or change the tie. Our guide to choosing and styling cardigans explains how the neckline and front opening shape the outfit.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: With a V-neck cardigan, the ends can follow the opening. If the cardigan is buttoned up, a large knot may sit directly over the buttons. Move it off-center or change the tie. Our guide to choosing and styling cardigans explains how the neckline and front opening shape the outfit.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Work with the neckline you’re wearing

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: With a high-collared jacket, zip it to where you’ll wear it before testing the scarf. A style that works with the jacket open may feel crowded with the collar closed. Use fewer wraps or a thinner scarf if the layers restrict head movement.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: With a high-collared jacket, zip it to where you’ll wear it before testing the scarf. A style that works with the jacket open may feel crowded with the collar closed. Use fewer wraps or a thinner scarf if the layers restrict head movement.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Work with the neckline you’re wearing

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: If you’re still choosing a base top, our item-by-item styling guide can help you find the main piece first. Use the scarf to add color or shape once the top fits comfortably on its own.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: If you’re still choosing a base top, our item-by-item styling guide can help you find the main piece first. Use the scarf to add color or shape once the top fits comfortably on its own.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Work with the neckline you’re wearing

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: Look at the ends while standing, sitting, and bending. Long tails can catch on a bag, zipper, or something you’re carrying. Change the wrap or choose a shorter scarf if the ends get in the way.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: Look at the ends while standing, sitting, and bending. Long tails can catch on a bag, zipper, or something you’re carrying. Change the wrap or choose a shorter scarf if the ends get in the way.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Check the ends and move around before going out

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: When riding or near moving parts, tuck the ends away and secure the scarf so nothing hangs near wheels or machinery. If you can’t secure it, take it off and stow it before moving. Choose a style that works for the activity.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: When riding or near moving parts, tuck the ends away and secure the scarf so nothing hangs near wheels or machinery. If you can’t secure it, take it off and stow it before moving. Choose a style that works for the activity.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Check the ends and move around before going out

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: If the scarf catches on an earring or button, stop and free the snag before pulling. After wearing, undo the knot gently, lay the scarf out to check it, and store it according to the care instructions. Loosen the knot fully before putting it away.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: If the scarf catches on an earring or button, stop and free the snag before pulling. After wearing, undo the knot gently, lay the scarf out to check it, and store it according to the care instructions. Loosen the knot fully before putting it away.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Check the ends and move around before going out

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: Start with two styles that suit the scarf you already own: a simple drape for busy days and a knotted style for a change. Once you can adjust the length, width, and room at the neck, those two styles can give you several looks.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: Start with two styles that suit the scarf you already own: a simple drape for busy days and a knotted style for a change. Once you can adjust the length, width, and room at the neck, those two styles can give you several looks.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Check the ends and move around before going out

en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.old: If the print is mainly at the ends, pick a style that leaves them visible. If the pattern runs throughout, one wrap can bring enough color close to the face. Try turning the scarf over before changing the knot. The design you want may simply be folded inward.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.text: If the print is mainly at the ends, pick a style that leaves them visible. If the pattern runs throughout, one wrap can bring enough color close to the face. Try turning the scarf over before changing the knot. The design you want may simply be folded inward.
en/blog/cach-that-khan-quang-co-dai-cho-.heading: Check the ends and move around before going out

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: The cuff is the band at the end of the sleeve. It may have a single button, adjustable buttons, an extended band, or other details. Above it there’s often a vent that lets the sleeve open so your hand can pass through. Check for a small button at the vent before folding.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: The cuff is the band at the end of the sleeve. It may have a single button, adjustable buttons, an extended band, or other details. Above it there’s often a vent that lets the sleeve open so your hand can pass through. Check for a small button at the vent before folding.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Check the cuff and sleeve vent before rolling

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Undo the cuff button and, if necessary, the vent button. Avoid forcing a closed sleeve up your arm. With decorative buttons that don’t open, a narrow sleeve, or an unusual elastic cuff, check whether the design lends itself to rolling first.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Undo the cuff button and, if necessary, the vent button. Avoid forcing a closed sleeve up your arm. With decorative buttons that don’t open, a narrow sleeve, or an unusual elastic cuff, check whether the design lends itself to rolling first.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Check the cuff and sleeve vent before rolling

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Check the starting length with your arm relaxed, then reach forward. An already short sleeve can end higher than you intended after several folds. With a very long sleeve, the roll can feel bulky even when folded neatly.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Check the starting length with your arm relaxed, then reach forward. An already short sleeve can end higher than you intended after several folds. With a very long sleeve, the roll can feel bulky even when folded neatly.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Check the cuff and sleeve vent before rolling

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: When shopping online, ask for the sleeve length, cuff construction, and upper-arm measurement if you need it. Our online sizing guide explains how to compare those measurements with a shirt that fits. A well-fitting sleeve is easier to work with than one you have to roll to correct its length.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: When shopping online, ask for the sleeve length, cuff construction, and upper-arm measurement if you need it. Our online sizing guide explains how to compare those measurements with a shirt that fits. A well-fitting sleeve is easier to work with than one you have to roll to correct its length.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Check the cuff and sleeve vent before rolling

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: This roll keeps the wrist clear for writing, using a computer, or wearing a watch. It can stop well below the elbow. A low fold that clears the wrist often holds its shape better than several higher folds on a narrow sleeve.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: This roll keeps the wrist clear for writing, using a computer, or wearing a watch. It can stop well below the elbow. A low fold that clears the wrist often holds its shape better than several higher folds on a narrow sleeve.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 1: A basic fold the width of the cuff

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: If the cuff is long, check whether the first fold sits too high. Try another method to control how much cuff shows, or leave the sleeve down and adjust the button. Folding a stiff cuff in half can leave a crease you didn’t want.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: If the cuff is long, check whether the first fold sits too high. Try another method to control how much cuff shows, or leave the sleeve down and adjust the button. Folding a stiff cuff in half can leave a crease you didn’t want.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 1: A basic fold the width of the cuff

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Repeat on the other sleeve, then compare both with your arms relaxed. The widths and positions can be close without matching to the millimeter. If one sits much higher because the sleeve twisted, unroll it and start again.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Repeat on the other sleeve, then compare both with your arms relaxed. The widths and positions can be close without matching to the millimeter. If one sits much higher because the sleeve twisted, unroll it and start again.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 1: A basic fold the width of the cuff

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Try this roll to show the inside of the cuff or get a defined two-layer look. Undo the buttons and smooth the sleeve. Turn the cuff up above where you want the roll to finish, leaving a length of sleeve fabric below the turned-up cuff.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Try this roll to show the inside of the cuff or get a defined two-layer look. Undo the buttons and smooth the sleeve. Turn the cuff up above where you want the roll to finish, leaving a length of sleeve fabric below the turned-up cuff.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 2: A roll that leaves part of the cuff showing

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Fold that fabric up over most of the cuff and leave as much of the edge showing as you like. Adjust the fold all the way around. Bend and straighten your arm to see whether the visible edge stays in place or slips inside the roll.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Fold that fabric up over most of the cuff and leave as much of the edge showing as you like. Adjust the fold all the way around. Bend and straighten your arm to see whether the visible edge stays in place or slips inside the roll.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 2: A roll that leaves part of the cuff showing

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: The starting height depends on the shirt. A narrow upper sleeve can feel tight before you even make the fold if you pull the cuff too high. Start low and move up only while you still have enough room to move.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: The starting height depends on the shirt. A narrow upper sleeve can feel tight before you even make the fold if you pull the cuff too high. Start low and move up only while you still have enough room to move.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 2: A roll that leaves part of the cuff showing

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: A contrasting cuff can become an accent in the outfit. If the shirt already has a large print, try showing a narrow edge. A matching cuff still gives the roll a different look through its fold and texture.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: A contrasting cuff can become an accent in the outfit. If the shirt already has a large print, try showing a narrow edge. A matching cuff still gives the roll a different look through its fold and texture.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 2: A roll that leaves part of the cuff showing

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: A slightly uneven fold can suit a relaxed outfit. Check that it stays where you want it and lets your arm move. Adjust the folds that are slipping and keep any variation you like.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: A slightly uneven fold can suit a relaxed outfit. Check that it stays where you want it and lets your arm move. Adjust the folds that are slipping and keep any variation you like.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 2: A roll that leaves part of the cuff showing

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: Try a higher roll only if the sleeve is wide enough where it will end. Make a basic fold first, then go higher in small steps and check the fit each time. If the roll ends right where your elbow bends, try moving it a little higher or lower to see what feels better.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: Try a higher roll only if the sleeve is wide enough where it will end. Make a basic fold first, then go higher in small steps and check the fit each time. If the roll ends right where your elbow bends, try moving it a little higher or lower to see what feels better.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 3: A higher roll when there’s enough room

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: If the roll feels tight, unfold a layer or move it down before trying to push it past the elbow. You should be able to bend your arm naturally. Deep marks, a pinching feeling, or having to hold your arm in one position are signs to adjust it.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: If the roll feels tight, unfold a layer or move it down before trying to push it past the elbow. You should be able to bend your arm naturally. Deep marks, a pinching feeling, or having to hold your arm in one position are signs to adjust it.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 3: A higher roll when there’s enough room

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: A higher roll adds more volume around the arm. On a very loose shirt, thick rolls can make the outfit feel heavy. Try fewer folds, a lighter shirt, or sleeves left down if the roll in your reference photo doesn’t suit your shirt.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: A higher roll adds more volume around the arm. On a very loose shirt, thick rolls can make the outfit feel heavy. Try fewer folds, a lighter shirt, or sleeves left down if the roll in your reference photo doesn’t suit your shirt.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 3: A higher roll when there’s enough room

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: If you wear the shirt as an outer layer, take it off and put it on again to see what happens. The folds may shift as your arms slide over the base layer. If you’ll put it on and take it off repeatedly, choose a roll that’s easy to redo.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: If you wear the shirt as an outer layer, take it off and put it on again to see what happens. The folds may shift as your arms slide over the base layer. If you’ll put it on and take it off repeatedly, choose a roll that’s easy to redo.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Method 3: A higher roll when there’s enough room

en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.old: A crisp shirt: Smooth each fold before making the next. Once it lies flat, leave the fabric loose enough to stay comfortable. A thick, stiff roll can make the wrist area look bulkier than you want.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.text: A crisp shirt: Smooth each fold before making the next. Once it lies flat, leave the fabric loose enough to stay comfortable. A thick, stiff roll can make the wrist area look bulkier than you want.
en/blog/cach-xan-tay-ao-so-mi-nu.html.heading: Adjust for surface texture and fabric weight

en/blog/chan-vay-do-do-ket-hop-voi-ao-ma.old: A burgundy skirt can work with several color families. Use lightness, finish, and proportions to narrow down the choices. Keep the outfits that suit your plans and let you move without frequent adjustments.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: Lay the skirt out in good light and step back. If the flowers blend into a single block, start with the color you see from a distance. If individual clusters stand out, try picking up a secondary color from the print in the top.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.heading: Look at the skirt’s background color first

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A black skirt with white flowers is easy to try with a white, black, or gray top. With blue flowers on cream, start with a cream or soft blue top. Picking up a color connects the pieces even when the shades differ slightly.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: A black skirt with white flowers is easy to try with a white, black, or gray top. With blue flowers on cream, start with a cream or soft blue top. Picking up a color connects the pieces even when the shades differ slightly.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.heading: Look at the skirt’s background color first

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A dense, bright floral print on a dark background can look busy even when the flowers are small. A plain top and simple neckline give the eye somewhere to rest. With a sparse, low-contrast print, a textured top can add interest without overwhelming it.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: A dense, bright floral print on a dark background can look busy even when the flowers are small. A plain top and simple neckline give the eye somewhere to rest. With a sparse, low-contrast print, a textured top can add interest without overwhelming it.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: Look at the print itself as well as the label. Our guide to ditsy floral dresses explains how print density works on a one-piece garment. With a separate skirt, you can choose a top that makes the print more or less prominent.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: Look at the print itself as well as the label. Our guide to ditsy floral dresses explains how print density works on a one-piece garment. With a separate skirt, you can choose a top that makes the print more or less prominent.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A white tee with a dark floral skirt is an easy combination to test. Pick a length you can tuck in or leave loose as you prefer. If the tee covers most of your hips, fold the hem up temporarily in front of a mirror to see whether you prefer the pieces to meet higher.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: A white tee with a dark floral skirt is an easy combination to test. Pick a length you can tuck in or leave loose as you prefer. en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A full tuck works when the fabric is fairly thin and the waistband has room. Tuck in the hem a section at a time, ease a little fabric out so you can move, and check from the side. Bunching at the stomach often comes from excess fabric or how the top is tucked.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: For an untucked look, try a boxy tee that ends near the waistband or upper hip. A straight hem creates a clear break across the print. A longer tee can give a relaxed proportion if the hem sits where you want it and stays put.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: For an untucked look, try a boxy tee that ends near the waistband or upper hip. A straight hem creates a clear break across the print. A longer tee can give a relaxed proportion if the hem sits where you want it and stays put.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: Sleeves add volume too. A wide sleeve with a full skirt has a different shape from a slim sleeve with a straight skirt. To keep attention on the skirt, try a slimmer sleeve before changing the color or adding a belt.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: Sleeves add volume too. A wide sleeve with a full skirt has a different shape from a slim sleeve with a straight skirt. To keep attention on the skirt, try a slimmer sleeve before changing the color or adding a belt.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: An ivory, pale blue, or background-colored button-up gives the outfit more structure than a tee. The buttons and collar already add detail, so ruffles, a large bow, or dense embroidery are optional. Try a neat tuck with a lightly flared skirt to show the waistband.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: An ivory, pale blue, or background-colored button-up gives the outfit more structure than a tee. en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: With a loose shirt, open the collar to a depth you like and adjust the sleeves to break up the upper half. If it has a long curved hem, see whether a partial tuck stays in place as you walk and sit.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A blouse with minimal ruffles can flow into a soft floral skirt. To distinguish the pieces, choose a top lighter than the skirt’s background or a matte blouse with a slightly glossy skirt. Two fabrics can drape similarly in different colors.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: With puff sleeves, keep the neckline and bodice fairly simple. The sleeves draw attention above and the floral print below. If you also want a large bow at the chest, try simpler earrings or a plain bag to give each detail room.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: Try a pale blue cardigan and cream base layer with a cream skirt printed with blue flowers. The cardigan repeats blue over a larger area, while the base layer picks up the background. If the layers are too warm for your plans, wear the cardigan in air-conditioned spaces and take it off when you need to.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.old: A long cardigan can work too, with more of the print covered. Wear it open with a fairly slim base layer and check how much print shows down the middle. A short cardigan usually leaves more of the skirt visible than a long, heavy one.
en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: A long cardigan can work too, with more of the print covered. Wear it open with a fairly slim base layer and check how much print shows down the middle. A short cardigan usually leaves more of the skirt visible than a long, heavy one.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: A long straight skirt with little flare can look relaxed with a roomy top. en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: With an elastic waist, check whether it stays where you want it when you sit and walk. If it rolls or twists, adjust the fit before covering it with a top. An untucked top can hide the waistband while the skirt still needs to feel stable on its own.

en/blog/chan-vay-hoa-nhi-dang-dai-phoi-v.text: Check top length from the front and side. A top can look neat from the front and bunch at the back. Stand naturally before deciding whether to tuck it, adjust the hem, or try another top.

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: Chicano style is a fashion vocabulary connected with Mexican-American and Chicano culture, often expressed through structured volume, workwear, button-ups or flannel, draped trousers and considered accessories. Begin with proportions and cultural context rather than stereotypes.

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: This guide moves from zoot suits and pachuco/pachuca history to silhouettes, foundational pieces and five contemporary women's outfit interpretations.

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: Chicano style in fashion often describes clothing inspired by Mexican-American and Chicano culture in the United States: controlled volume, workwear, shirts or flannel, draped mid- or high-rise trousers, denim, white tees or tanks, substantial shoes and selected accessories. Baggy clothing, a bandana and flannel alone overlook its cultural context and proportional relationships.

Baggy clothing, a bandana and flannel alone overlook its cultural context and proportional relationships.
en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.heading: What Is Chicano Style?

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: No single item defines the look. Consider the silhouette: a structured or layered upper half, room through the lower half, a readable waist and footwear that anchors the combination. Contemporary women's interpretations can retain these relationships without reproducing a historical image as a costume.

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: Zoot suits help explain the significance of volume. In the late 1930s and early 1940s, broad shoulders, long jackets and very full trousers tapering at the ankles became prominent across several US communities of color. PBS and Smithsonian describe their popularity among Black and Latino youth; in Los Angeles, they became closely associated with Mexican-American pachuco culture.

PBS and Smithsonian describe their popularity among Black and Latino youth; in Los Angeles, they became closely associated with Mexican-American pachuco culture.
en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.heading: From Zoot Suits to Contemporary Chicano References

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: Remember that the zoot suit does not have one exclusively Chicano origin story. It circulated across communities, while pachuco and pachuca clothing became powerful expressions of Mexican-American presence and self-definition. During Los Angeles's 1943 Zoot Suit Riots, Mexican-American young people were attacked, with clothing used as a marker for targeting them.

The Los Angeles Times describes pencil skirts with broad-shouldered jackets as well as wide trousers. Contemporary interpretation can learn from proportion and construction rather than reconstructing an entire 1940s outfit.

en/blog/chicano-style-history-outfits.ht.old: Do not equate Chicano style with gangster style. Pachuco clothing was historically criminalized in media and official discourse; PBS and historical research describe how conspicuous dress became a pretext for discrimination against Mexican-American youth. Context explains why the clothing carries significance beyond a visual trend.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: A soft surface alone won’t establish that chiffon is silk, and Vietnamese fabrics sold as “voan” can differ. If a seller combines several terms, ask what the fabric contains and which part of the garment uses it.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: A label that only says “silk chiffon” may leave you without the fiber information you need for care. Feel, sheen, and price won’t establish composition. A clear photo of the label tells you more than terms such as “premium” or “cool to the touch.”

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Hold the fabric against a light and a dark background to see what shows. For a finished top, try it with the underlayer you’ll wear. Fitting-room lights and daylight by a window can reveal different levels of sheerness.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Printed chiffon can still be sheer. Check between the printed motifs and around the placket and side seams. Decide how much coverage you want for the occasion and check it before leaving.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Hold up part of the fabric and let it fall naturally. For a layered skirt, walk to see how each layer moves. Gathering, pleats, and ruffles give chiffon a different silhouette from a plain cut.
en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.text: Hold up part of the fabric and let it fall naturally. For a layered skirt, walk to see how each layer moves. Gathering, pleats, and ruffles give chiffon a different silhouette from a plain cut.
en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.heading: Does it drape or hold its shape?

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Extra layers can add volume at the waist, shoulders, or sleeves. If you want a light silhouette, check how much fabric collects where the layers join.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.heading: Does it drape or hold its shape?

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Check the seams, rolled edges, closures, and embellishments. If you see a pulled thread or distorted edge, ask the seller about it before accepting the item. A small irregularity on lightweight fabric can be visible when worn.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.heading: Look and feel where the garment touches you

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: With a chiffon dress, see where the lining starts and ends. A long outer layer may come with a shorter lining. Try sitting and walking to see how the two layers shift.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.heading: Check what the lining changes

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: A chiffon top can have an attached liner or work with a separate layer underneath. Choose a neckline and straps that suit the outer top. If the underlayer has a visible edge, decide whether you want it to show.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.heading: Check what the lining changes

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: A shade close to your skin and a shade close to the top give different effects. Compare them under the actual top, since the contrast depends on its color and sheerness. White underneath white may still be visible.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Check whether the straps, side seams, or hems catch on each other. If you keep adjusting them, try an underlayer with a different length or finish. Keep the combination light and easy to move in if that’s the goal.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Loose blouse: Try structured trousers to contrast with the soft fabric. Check the hem tucked and untucked. If the fabric bunches at the waist, try another tuck or a shorter top.

en/blog/chiffon-la-vai-gi.html.old: Puff sleeves or layered sleeves: Try them with a jacket and bag. Sleeves that fall nicely on their own can bunch in a narrow jacket. Test the layers together if that’s how you’ll dress.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: Choosing a bag for an outfit starts with use, then proportion, shape, surface and hardware, and finally color. A matching color cannot resolve unsuitable capacity or an unwanted strap position.
en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.text: Choosing a bag for an outfit starts with use, then proportion, shape, surface and hardware, and finally color. A matching color cannot resolve unsuitable capacity or an unwanted strap position.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: This guide focuses on alternative and dark fashion, while its principles of silhouette, visual weight, texture, and use also apply to everyday clothing.
en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.text: This guide focuses on alternative and dark fashion, while its principles of silhouette, visual weight, texture, and use also apply to everyday clothing.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: Before choosing by color, follow five steps: what to carry → clothing volume → soft or structured bag → existing focal details → color. This helps distinguish a color match from a bag whose scale and role actually serve the outfit.
en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.text: Before choosing by color, follow five steps: what to carry → clothing volume → soft or structured bag → existing focal details → color . This helps distinguish a color match from a bag whose scale and role actually serve the outfit.
en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.heading: A Thirty-Second Bag Choice

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: A bag need not follow a fixed body-size rule. Inspect its relationship with clothing and carrying position. A roomy top, cargos, and substantial shoes already create several larger areas. A large soft tote adds more volume; a compact shoulder bag or crossbody can provide a quieter contrast.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.heading: 1. Compare Bag and Clothing Proportions

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: A fitted top and straight jeans can also carry a larger bag if contrast is intended. Do not choose a small bag solely because the wearer is small; assess its area within the whole silhouette.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.heading: 1. Compare Bag and Clothing Proportions

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: A crossbody ending at the waist differs from one dropping toward the thigh. Waist-level carrying draws attention to the middle; a lower hip position extends the diagonal. A long strap can obscure a crop or corset-inspired waist, while a very short one can crowd a longer jacket's lapel area. Adjust around the actual layers.

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.heading: 2. Strap Length Places the Visual Break

en/blog/choosing-bags-for-alternative-ou.old: A structured bag holds clearer edges and can contrast with soft draping clothing or continue existing tailored lines. A hobo or slouchy bag adds a softer relaxed outline beside denim, knit, or roomy tees. A baguette or compact shoulder bag stays closer to the upper body and can contrast with fuller trousers or skirts.

en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.old: White dots on black create clear contrast and pair easily with black shoes or a light bag. For a softer look, try cream dots on brown or small dots on deep blue. Check the actual shade because cream, ivory, and bright white can look quite different.

en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.old: On a straight dress, the print can run from shoulder to hem with few breaks. Highlight the neckline or shoes if you prefer to leave the waist unbelted. If you add a tie, check for bunching and see whether it changes the hem on either side.
en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.text: On a straight dress, the print can run from shoulder to hem with few breaks. Highlight the neckline or shoes if you prefer to leave the waist unbelted. If you add a tie, check for bunching and see whether it changes the hem on either side.

en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.text: With a gently fitted cut, see whether dots stretch out of shape at the bust or hips. Walk and sit to check seams, tension, and coverage. Try another cut if a larger size gives extra room in the wrong areas.

en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.old: A row of buttons draws a straight line through the pattern. With large contrasting buttons, simple jewelry works near the neckline. With a wrap, check the overlap when bending or sitting as well as standing.
en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.text: A row of buttons draws a straight line through the pattern. With large contrasting buttons, simple jewelry works near the neckline. With a wrap, check the overlap when bending or sitting as well as standing.

en/blog/dam-cham-bi-co-dien.html.heading: Check how much detail the neckline and sleeves add

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: Light flowers stand out against a dark ground, while a pale print on a light ground may feel softer. Try a scattered or low-contrast print if you want something subtle. If you want the print to lead, try simple shoes and a bag so the pattern remains easy to see.

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.heading: Choose the cut before the style label

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: Ruching, ruffles, and puff sleeves add volume alongside the print. For a simpler silhouette, choose which area you want to highlight. If you like puff sleeves with florals, check whether your hair, earrings, and neckline leave enough room for those details to show.
en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.heading: Choose the cut before the style label

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.old: Our guide to choosing dresses by shape and length helps you compare different cuts. Here the focus is a small floral print on a one-piece dress. A floral skirt worn with a separate top has different proportions because the print doesn’t extend across the whole outfit.

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: With a short dress, check coverage while sitting and stepping up. A length you like in the mirror can shift when you carry a bag or reach. Choose the coverage you feel comfortable with in the setting where you’ll wear it.

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: A midi ends somewhere between the knee and ankle, depending on the dress and your height. Look at the gap between the hem and the shoes. If the hem and shoe tops both create strong horizontal lines, try a more streamlined shoe or a different dress length.

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: Try a long dress with the exact shoes you’ll wear. You should be able to walk on ordinary surfaces without lifting the hem the whole time. Before shortening it, check how the alteration would affect a border, the print placement, or a tier.

en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: A slit gives your legs room to move and reveals more of them as you walk. Take a few steps, sit down, and turn sideways to see how far the slit opens. en/blog/dam-hoa-nhi.html.text: Front, side, and off-center slits draw the eye differently. A high slit can add another focal point to a high-contrast floral print. If you like both details, keep the shoes and bag simple so the outfit remains easy to take in.

en/blog/denim-on-denim.html.heading: Keep a repeatable formula and change one variable

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.old: If traveling by motorbike, consider the journey and weather too. An open sandal may work for a city stroll but does not provide the coverage of closed shoes. No sandal suits every condition simply because it has thick soles or broad straps.

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.heading: Choose for your plans before choosing strap style

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.old: Thin straps expose more skin and often look lighter in a full-length view. When trying them, check whether straps lie flat or twist along the edges. A narrow but rigid strap in a friction-prone spot can still be uncomfortable despite a light sole.

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.heading: Thin straps and low soles: light lines

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.old: These can work with neat straight-leg trousers, dresses or skirts with few tiers. Very loose, layered clothing may visually overwhelm delicate sandals. Try a wider strap or more contrasting color rather than necessarily increasing sole height.

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.heading: Thin straps and low soles: light lines

en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.old: Broad straps create visible areas across the instep and often suit structured outfits. Check contact points, stitched edges and adjustment range. If the front presses into your foot while the back strap remains loose, tightening the back will not solve the front's fit problem.
en/blog/dep-quai-hau-nu.html.text: Broad straps create visible areas across the instep and often suit structured outfits. Check contact points, stitched edges and adjustment range.
